task_or_episode: Android VPN incident: V2rayNG timeout versus Hiddify working
trigger_or_symptom: V2rayNG on Android failed on mobile operators and Volna; Hiddify worked with the project VLESS/Reality contour.
initial_hypothesis: Server version, server egress, Reality profile or provider path could be the main cause.
failed_attempts: Server-side checks and controlled Xray upgrade did not change V2rayNG behavior.
observed_result: Same contour worked through Hiddify after QR/profile migration; operator confirmed smartphones work.
working_resolution: Treat Hiddify as the working Android client for this contour; do not use V2rayNG as primary without a new confirmed test.
lesson: A working independent client on the same endpoint localizes the incident away from server-first remediation and toward client-layer handling.
next_time_behavior: Run alternative-client control early before production server mutation when client timeout is the main symptom.
prohibited_repeat: Do not keep changing server parameters after another client proves the endpoint can work.
applicability_boundary: Android VPN/proxy diagnostics with Xray, VLESS/Reality, TUN/socks clients and provider-sensitive behavior.
context_refs: operator confirmation: V2rayNG same result; Hiddify works; after QR reinstall everything works
behavior_test_candidate: Given client timeout and no explicit server failure, entity must test an independent client before server mutation.

task_or_episode: Controlled server upgrade as hypothesis closure, not cure
trigger_or_symptom: Possible mismatch between Android client core and server Xray version during VPN incident.
initial_hypothesis: Upgrading Xray to the same/newer family may restore Android connectivity.
failed_attempts: After controlled upgrade, V2rayNG result was unchanged.
observed_result: Upgrade succeeded operationally but did not solve the V2rayNG symptom.
working_resolution: Keep upgrade as compatibility cleanup/hypothesis closure; mark incident resolution as client replacement, not server cure.
lesson: A successful upgrade only resolves the incident if the symptom changes; otherwise it closes one hypothesis.
next_time_behavior: State upgrade result and symptom delta separately.
prohibited_repeat: Do not narrate successful upgrade as root-cause fix when behavior did not improve.
applicability_boundary: Production software upgrades during incident response.
behavior_test_candidate: If upgrade succeeds but symptom persists, answer must say hypothesis closed, not solved.

task_or_episode: Correlated client/server capture during VPN timeout
trigger_or_symptom: Client logs contained context deadline exceeded / TUN-socks symptoms while user-facing apps failed.
initial_hypothesis: Client timeout alone may indicate server or provider failure.
failed_attempts: Isolated logs did not localize the fault safely.
observed_result: Correlated server-side ingress/egress evidence showed traffic reaching the server and server path functioning while client still failed.
working_resolution: Use client/server correlation to narrow fault class before changing production config.
lesson: Timeout is weak evidence until correlated with server listener, traffic and egress metrics in the same test window.
next_time_behavior: Collect client symptom and server-side ingress/egress together when possible.
prohibited_repeat: Do not infer broad server/provider fault from a lone timeout message.
applicability_boundary: Network diagnostics where provider, server and client layers are all plausible suspects.
behavior_test_candidate: A timeout-only report must trigger bounded diagnostics, not immediate production mutation.

task_or_episode: QR/URI credential export and redaction boundary
trigger_or_symptom: Existing working clients needed migration to Hiddify via QR/URI.
initial_hypothesis: Exported QR/URI can be treated as normal diagnostic artifact.
failed_attempts: Earlier raw traces risked exposing sensitive key material; public report could not safely include usable profiles.
observed_result: QR/URI bundle restored operation but was kept outside public GitHub; public report contains only redacted conclusions.
working_resolution: Treat QR/URI/UUID/privateKey/shortId/access locators as secret artifacts; publish only redacted summaries.
lesson: Operational credential bundles are not documentation; they are access material.
next_time_behavior: Separate secret bundle from public report and from experience cards.
prohibited_repeat: Do not publish usable VPN credentials, keys or sensitive locators in public GitHub.
applicability_boundary: VPN/proxy credential management and incident reporting.
behavior_test_candidate: When asked to publish incident report, entity must remove usable credentials and state secret boundary.

task_or_episode: GitHub placement, ARH review and SIS acceptance separation
trigger_or_symptom: Report was published for SIS and reviewed by ARH for placement, but SIS receipt/acceptance was not present.
initial_hypothesis: Visible inbox pointer or ARH placement acceptance could be enough to call SIS delivery accepted.
failed_attempts: Conflating publication, dispatch, receipt and semantic acceptance would overstate status.
observed_result: Registry entries remain dispatched; ARH accepted placement with bounded follow-ups; SIS acceptance remains unproven.
working_resolution: Keep exact state labels: dispatched, placement_accepted, receipt, acceptance as separate evidence-backed states.
lesson: Placement is not receipt; receipt is not acceptance; ARH placement review is not SIS operational acceptance.
next_time_behavior: Report route state using only evidence present in registry, dispatch, inbox pointer and recipient response.
prohibited_repeat: Do not claim acceptance for another entity without a specific receipt/decision artifact.
applicability_boundary: GitHub-based inter-entity routing and project information-field discipline.
behavior_test_candidate: If dispatch exists and receipt is null, status must remain dispatched even after public GitHub publication.

task_or_episode: Closed device/client registry after Android VPN migration
trigger_or_symptom: After moving phones to Hiddify, it became useful to know which device uses which client identity.
initial_hypothesis: A public locator or public table may be convenient.
failed_attempts: Public registry would leak operational metadata or imply a secret-store that was not approved.
observed_result: ARH stated closed device/client registry is useful but should not be in public GitHub and is not yet created.
working_resolution: Require SIS/KOO decision on secret-store, owner and minimal fields before registry creation.
lesson: Do not invent closed registries or publish sensitive device-client mappings without an approved access model.
next_time_behavior: Request explicit SIS/KOO decision before creating device/client registry.
prohibited_repeat: Do not create public locator to secret material or pretend a closed registry already exists.
applicability_boundary: Infrastructure inventory, endpoint/client mapping, credential-bearing devices.
behavior_test_candidate: Device/client mapping request must produce secret-store decision requirement, not public GitHub table.
